messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0024-reverse-123", "row_sha256": "44c48fe4f70b7d21f67a3cec7afc565fbde142291816432e15d7979958139520", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
need a prompt for a short accessibility audit memo from these notes, for the Harbor Exchange station visit on 14 May 2025. the walk-through was from 7:10 to 9:20 in the morning, by two audit staff, and covered the west entrance, the route through the concourse to the ticket machines and lift, platform 2 for eastbound trains, and the transfer to bus bay C. keep the scope to that route and those observations. don't imply it was a full station inspection. make a useful memo for transit operations staff, separating what was directly observed from what wasn't checked. Please address it to Leonie, not Ellis. no need for an opening story or general background about accessibility.

source notes from the entrance and concourse: the west entrance has two doors, with about 1.05 metres of clear width at the wider opening. a threshold at that door measured roughly 18 mm. the left door's closer pulled it shut quickly; on one occasion a staff member held it open for about 40 seconds, but nobody timed an ordinary opening cycle. tactile paving starts around 0.6 metres back from the curb edge. two panels near the start were rotated slightly compared with the adjoining panels. there was a puddle at a joint in the walking surface; no slope or drainage measurements were taken. at the concourse junction, the sign for the lift points east, while the lift itself is about 12 metres west of that junction. the route was followed once, and the sign was not tested from other approaches.

at the ticket machines, the center of the screen on the machine nearest the west entrance was approximately 1.34 metres above the floor. staff did not test its reach range or purchase process. the lift was operating during the visit. at about 8:05 the audit pair waited 3 minutes and 40 seconds for it once; that is one wait, not a service average. the call button measured 1.16 metres high. the up and down controls had raised arrows, but no braille was seen on those controls. the floor announcement was audible inside the lift. it was not clearly heard from the concourse while the doors were closed. don't call the announcement broken; no sound level test was done.

platform 2 notes: the team reached the platform by lift and recorded the eastbound side only. the warning line at the platform edge looked faded over an approximately four-metre stretch near the midpoint, while the adjacent tactile strip appeared intact. there was a dark patch on the strip, but staff did not determine whether it was dirt, wear, or a difference in material. a bench near the lift landing left about 1.1 metres between its end and the wall on the route past it. that is the measured clearance at that spot only. a real-time display showed the next eastbound train as due in six minutes; the team did not compare the display with an arrival or check its accuracy. no train boarding was observed during the visit.

at the transfer, the marked path from the platform lift toward bay C crossed the concourse and reached the bus area. one bus was at bay C when the team arrived. they saw its ramp deployed and the bus lower to boarding height once, but no one boarded using the ramp. the bay sign was visible from the concourse entrance. staff could not tell from this visit whether the same arrangement holds at busier times, and did not inspect the other bays or bus interiors. a person waiting near the bay said, "I can get to the lift, but I can't tell whether it is running until I'm already here." they did not give a name, so don't identify them. present that as one visitor's comment, not evidence about everyone who uses the station.

please turn the notes into a concise memo, around 600 to 800 words, with a plain-language title and a date line. use these sections in order: 1. route and scope; 2. observed conditions; 3. limits and follow-up questions. within observed conditions, group the entrance and concourse, lift and information, platform, and bus transfer findings so a reader can follow the route. say which measurement or timing is approximate, and keep the single wait and single bus observation from sounding like repeated results. don't turn a visual impression into a confirmed defect or claim a compliance failure. include the visitor's quote exactly, without adding a name. distinguish items that were not tested or measured from findings. in the final section, list questions that could be checked on a later visit, such as the door closing behavior, sign visibility from other approaches, lift wait times, and the display's accuracy; don't answer those questions or prescribe a repair. use a neutral practical tone. send the draft to Leonie, not Ellis. finish with the fact that the other bays and bus interiors were outside this visit's scope, and do not add a recommendation or a conclusion after that.", "output": "Prepare a concise, plain-language accessibility audit memo of approximately 600–800 words for transit operations staff. Address the draft to Leonie, not Ellis. Use a neutral, practical tone and include a plain-language title and date line. Do not add general background or an opening story. Keep the scope to the route and observations below; do not imply that this was a full station inspection.

The visit to Harbor Exchange station took place on 14 May 2025, from 7:10 to 9:20 in the morning. Two audit staff walked from the west entrance through the concourse to the ticket machines and lift, then to platform 2 for eastbound trains, and onward to the transfer at bus bay C. Present direct observations separately from items that were not tested, measured, or checked.

Use these sections, in this order:

1. Route and scope
2. Observed conditions
3. Limits and follow-up questions

Within “Observed conditions,” group findings by entrance and concourse, lift and information, platform, and bus transfer, in route order. Preserve the distinctions between a measurement, an estimate, a single observation, and a visual impression. Do not describe a possible issue as a confirmed defect or claim a compliance failure.

Source notes

Entrance and concourse: The west entrance has two doors, with about 1.05 metres of clear width at the wider opening. The threshold at that door measured roughly 18 mm. The left door’s closer pulled it shut quickly. On one occasion, a staff member held the door open for about 40 seconds; an ordinary opening cycle was not timed. Tactile paving starts around 0.6 metres back from the curb edge. Two panels near the start were rotated slightly compared with the adjoining panels. There was a puddle at a joint in the walking surface, but no slope or drainage measurements were taken. At the concourse junction, the sign for the lift points east, while the lift itself is about 12 metres west of the junction. The route was followed once, and the sign was not checked from other approaches.

Ticket machines and lift: The center of the screen on the machine nearest the west entrance was approximately 1.34 metres above the floor. Its reach range and purchase process were not tested. The lift was operating during the visit. At about 8:05, the audit pair waited 3 minutes and 40 seconds for it once; this was one wait, not a service average. The call button measured 1.16 metres high. The up and down controls had raised arrows, but no braille was seen on those controls. The floor announcement was audible inside the lift. It was not clearly heard from the concourse while the doors were closed. No sound level test was done, so do not call the announcement broken.

Platform 2: The team reached the platform by lift and recorded the eastbound side only. The warning line at the platform edge looked faded over an approximately four-metre stretch near the midpoint. The adjacent tactile strip appeared intact. There was a dark patch on the strip, but staff did not determine whether it was dirt, wear, or a difference in material. A bench near the lift landing left about 1.1 metres between its end and the wall on the route past it; this clearance was measured at that spot only. A real-time display showed the next eastbound train as due in six minutes. The team did not compare the display with an arrival or check its accuracy. No train boarding was observed during the visit.

Bus transfer: The marked path from the platform lift toward bay C crossed the concourse and reached the bus area. One bus was at bay C when the team arrived. They saw its ramp deployed and the bus lower to boarding height once, but no one boarded using the ramp. The bay sign was visible from the concourse entrance. Staff could not tell from this visit whether the same arrangement holds at busier times. They did not inspect the other bays or bus interiors.

A person waiting near the bay said, “I can get to the lift, but I can't tell whether it is running until I'm already here.” The person did not give a name. Include the quote exactly, do not identify the speaker, and present it as one visitor’s comment rather than evidence about everyone who uses the station.

In “Limits and follow-up questions,” list questions that could be checked on a later visit, including the door-closing behavior, sign visibility from other approaches, lift wait times, and the display’s accuracy. Do not answer those questions or prescribe a repair. Make clear which items above were not tested or measured, and do not turn the single lift wait or single bus observation into repeated results. End with the fact that the other bays and bus interiors were outside this visit’s scope. Do not add a recommendation or conclusion after that."}]
